title: Nonclosed points in finite-type schemes have infinitely many closed specializations
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $z\in X$ is not closed, then the closure $\overline{\{z\}}$ contains infinitely many closed points of $X$ [def-weil-closed-points].

source.place: Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), together with Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), which gives positive dimension for the closure of a nonclosed point and hence infinitely many closed specializations
